bull.b: Broader adoption across product lines can deepen customer relationships and increase revenue per account, making growth less dependent on a single offering. If sustained, this mix shift may improve commercial efficiency and support more durable hospital and clinical-channel penetration.

Bringing Neox and Clarix production in-house could reduce the current reliance on higher transfer pricing and create a structural path to better gross margins. The opportunity is not yet realized, but successful validation and regulatory execution could materially improve operating leverage.

GPO access can lower procurement friction and expand the number of hospitals able to purchase VENDAJE through established contracts. This provides a durable commercial channel that may support broader product adoption and improve the scalability of the hospital-focused growth strategy.

bear.b: The sharp reduction in cash alongside rising operating cash use indicates that current operations are consuming liquidity faster than before. This constrains flexibility over the next several quarters and increases dependence on financing, collections, or other measures to sustain execution.

Deep TTM losses across both accounting and cash measures show that the business is not currently funding itself through operations. The swing from positive 2024 results to substantial losses raises execution risk and could delay the point at which growth investments translate into sustainable earnings.

Higher transfer pricing is compressing gross margin before the planned manufacturing transition is completed, limiting near-term contribution from revenue growth. Because management expects this pressure to persist until successful transfer, margin recovery remains dependent on execution and regulatory validation.
